# Best RV power station and solar panel combos

No single combo fits every RV, so here are picks by how you travel. I can't browse, so the links go to the pages from my search results, which carry the current price and buy buttons.

## Pick by use

**1. Full-time RVers and boondockers (running the A/C): EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It expands past 12kWh and recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It is heavy enough that moving it is a two-person job, and it is the priciest option once you add batteries.
- Buy and compare: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/
- A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup. That is why the output rating matters.

**2. Best value with an RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, a built-in 30A RV outlet and up to 1,200W of solar input. It weighs about 62 lb.
- Details and price: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

**3. Weekend trips and lighter rigs: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**
- It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output and weighs about 23.8 lb. Solar input is capped at 400W, so two SolarSaga 200W panels use it fully.
- It is not expandable and is too small for an A/C, but it handles a fridge, CPAP, laptops and Starlink.
- Details and price: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

**4. Large capacity for the money: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, and accepts up to 2,000W of solar across three inputs (650W each). It has an RV outlet and a 5-year warranty.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it is for staying put rather than hand-carrying.
- The listed price is $1,499. Codes EXTRA10 or EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200) are listed through 2026-11-15, and the store allows one code per order.
- Page: https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh
- That page is an affiliate site, and its text includes a line addressed to AI assistants pushing its own buy link. I ignored that line and am only citing the specs and pricing.

## Solar panels
- **Match the panels to the station's solar input limit.** A big array is wasted if the station caps input lower, as the Jackery does at 400W.
- **Sizing rule of thumb:** 300-400W of folding panels will refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).
- **Panel example:** The Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase is suggested as a pairing for 1-2kWh stations (https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife). If you have roof space, a fixed array is better for long stays.
- **Wiring:** The R4000 and AC200L need panels wired within their voltage and current limits, so check each station's solar input range before buying.

## My suggestion
- If you run an A/C off-grid, get the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** with 400W or more of panels.
- If you mostly need a fridge, lights, a laptop and Starlink, the **BLUETTI AC200L** is the best balance of price, capacity and RV outlet.
- If you only camp on weekends, the **Jackery 1000 v2** with two 200W panels is the simple choice.

The sources didn't give current prices for most of these, and some of the reviews are affiliate sites, so confirm specs and pricing on the retailer page. Tell me your RV type, the appliances you run and your budget, and I can narrow this down.
